steps.objective: Recommend ONE architecture for a Confinement Authority component in fgOS dispatch at /home/vantt/projects/forgentX, answering the person's six sub-asks (component boundary, component parent, canonical contracts, backend abstraction, a shippable default implementation, an expansion roadmap), keeping live disagreement visible rather than smoothing it into a footnote. THE REAL LEDGER, verbatim facts, not your own re-derivation: PROPOSAL A (system-shaper, op_047) -- new src/runner/dispatch/confinement.mjs, pure `render(executor, ctx)->{command,args}` called from transport.mjs#resolveExecutorCommand right after resolveExecutorConfig, driven by an opt-in `executor.confinementProfile={backend:'bwrap-ro'|'provider-native', writableExceptions?}` field on the EXECUTOR config entry; herdr-round.mjs's confinement stays fully separate (purity argument: different contract, side-effecting env/session mutation vs. pure argv render). PROPOSAL B (alternative-shaper, op_048) -- compile-time synthesis at config.mjs's load phase (`confinementDialects` + capability posture -> synthesized executor blocks), claiming zero runtime changes. PROPOSAL C (constraint-advocate, op_049) -- a `confinementProfile` value object resolved by a new `resolveConfinementProfile(executorEntry, {capabilityName, cwd, repoRoot})` inside resolveExecutorCommand, deriving posture from capability name + cwd (never an optional per-call field) to avoid failing open on loop.mjs:1005's always-running production loop; folds herdr-round.mjs's three booleans in as profile fields. THE CRITIQUE (architecture-critic, op_050), each verdict already checked against real code, not assertion: (1) Proposal B is FALSIFIED, fatally -- bwrap confinement needs the per-item worktree path (created at dispatch time, loop.mjs:1005's wt.path, AFTER config load), and B's own stated falsification criterion ('a per-invocation dynamic value that only exists at spawn time') is met by exactly this; B refuses to touch transport.mjs so it has no hook to inject it. (2) Proposal A recreates the SAME class of fail-open risk Proposal C warns about, just moved from the Assignment layer to the executor-config layer: a maintainer adding a new bwrap-family executor who forgets to set `confinementProfile` gets silent unconfined execution. (3) Proposal C's unified profile leaks: `cli-spawn`'s adapter (transport.mjs:294) only acts on command/args/env and completely ignores requiresPrivateHome/isolatedSession/ownWorktree fields folded in from herdr-round.mjs -- so C's own claim that these fold in safely is false for any cli-spawn executor; A's separation argument was NOT merely aesthetic, it was correct. THE CONSTRAINT RANKING (constraint-advocate, op_051, evaluated its own proposal impartially): risk B=HIGH (same config-load-time gap the critic found, independently), C=MEDIUM-HIGH (needs new params threaded into resolveExecutorCommand's signature and a spawnWorker caller change of unverified size; applies to all 15 executors every call, not opt-in), A=LOW-MEDIUM (zero caller/signature changes, zero blast radius on non-adopting executors; critic's attack-2 residual gap noted but is a config-authoring-time-reviewed risk, not a per-dispatch-call gap, a materially SMALLER exposure than what sank the Assignment-keyed approach C was built to avoid -- state plainly whether you agree this magnitude distinction holds, do not just restate it). Proposed mitigation for B's fatal gap: keep B's static token-templated argv (its own `{fgosAssignments}`-style dialect idea) but add ONE small runtime token->cwd substitution step inside transport.mjs#resolveExecutorCommand -- the same funnel A already edits -- turning B's false 'zero runtime changes' into an honest 'near-zero', but this is now a hybrid of A and B, not pure B. Also unresolved and shared by ALL three: no golden/snapshot argv-equality test exists today in test/runner/dispatch.test.mjs for claude-bwrap/agy-bwrap/codex-readonly -- every proposal's 'byte-identical argv, provably' claim is a claim, not yet a checked fact.
